chapterNote: The psalm of the King's entrance, written for a procession — very likely the day David brought the ark up to Zion with shouting and trumpets (2 Samuel 6), sung antiphonally, choirs answering choirs at the gates. Three movements. First the deed of ownership: the earth is the LORD's and everything that fills it, founded on the seas He mastered. Then the gate-question every worshiper must face: who may ascend the hill of the LORD? — and the answer searches hands, heart, soul, and tongue: clean hands, a pure heart, no soul lifted to emptiness, no oath sworn to deceive. Whoever seeks that face receives blessing and righteousness from the God of his salvation. Finally the great antiphon at the doors: Lift up your heads, O gates, that the King of glory may come in! — Who is this King of glory? — and the answer builds through the LORD mighty in battle to the final trumpet-blast title, the LORD of Hosts, He is the King of glory. The church has always sung it twice over: at the ascension, when the everlasting doors of heaven lifted for the returning conquering Christ, and at every heart's gate where the same King stands and knocks.

1.text: A psalm of David. The earth belongs to the LORD, with all its fullness — the world, and all who dwell in it.
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of David. The earth [eretz] is the LORD'S [YHWH], and the fulness [melo — all that fills it] thereof; the world [tebel], and they that dwell [yashab] therein.
1.notes: The title deed of the universe in one line: eretz and its melo (H4393), everything that fills it, the tebel (H8398) and its tenants. Paul cites it to free the Christian conscience at the meat market — everything on the table is the Lord's (cf. 1 Corinthians 10:26).

2.text: For He founded it upon the seas, and fixed it firm upon the currents beneath.
2.amp: For He has founded [yasad] it upon the seas [yam], and established [kun] it upon the floods [nahar — the rivers, the deep currents].
2.notes: The ownership rests on the founding: yasad and kun (H3245, H3559), the architect's verbs. The dry land standing stable over yam and nahar (H3220, H5104) — chaos-waters mastered into a foundation — is creation's own proof of who holds the deed (cf. Genesis 1:9-10).

3.text: Who may go up the mountain of the LORD, and who may stand in His holy place?
3.amp: Who shall ascend [alah] into the hill [har] of the LORD [YHWH]? or who shall stand [qum] in His holy [qodesh] place [maqom]?
3.notes: The gate-liturgy's question: alah (H5927) is the pilgrim's climbing-verb, qum (H6965) the standing that survives arrival. If all the earth is His (v. 1), the qodesh maqom is His supremely — and open ground for no one unexamined.

4.text: The one with clean hands and a pure heart, who has not lifted up his soul to what is empty and false, and has not sworn an oath to deceive.
4.amp: He that has clean [naqi — innocent] hands [kaph], and a pure [bar] heart [lebab]; who has not lifted up [nasa] his soul [nephesh] unto vanity [shav — emptiness, falsehood], and has not sworn [shaba] deceitfully [mirmah].
4.notes: Four checkpoints, outside in: kaph naqi (H3709, H5355), the deeds; lebab bar (H3824, H1249), the motives; the nephesh not nasa (H5375), not lifted, toward shav (H7723), the empty idols and lies; and the tongue's oaths free of mirmah (H4820). The standard is total — which is why verse 5 speaks of receiving, not achieving.

5.text: He will carry away blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God who saves him.
5.amp: He shall receive [nasa — lift away, carry off] the blessing [berakah] from the LORD [YHWH], and righteousness [tsedaqah] from the God [Elohim] of his salvation [yesha].
5.notes: The same verb turned inside out: the soul not lifted (nasa) to emptiness now lifts away berakah (H1293) from the LORD's hand. And the tsedaqah (H6666) comes FROM the Elohim of his yesha — righteousness received as gift from the saving God, not carried up the hill as luggage (cf. Philippians 3:9).

6.text: Such is the generation of the seekers, of those who search out Your face, O God of Jacob. Selah.
6.amp: This is the generation [dor] of them that seek [darash] Him, that seek [baqash] your face [panim], O Jacob ['O God of Jacob', the KJV margin]. Selah [selah].
6.notes: The climbers are defined not by attainment but by direction: darash and baqash (H1875, H1245), the double seeking, aimed at the panim (H6440) — the face, the presence itself. A whole dor (H1755) marked as seekers, the company of Psalm 27:8.

7.text: Lift up your heads, O you gates! Be lifted up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in!
7.amp: Lift up [nasa] your heads [rosh], O ye gates [shaar]; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting [olam] doors [petach]; and the King [melek] of glory [kabod] shall come in [bo].
7.notes: The procession reaches the walls and commands the architecture: gates ordered to nasa their rosh — lintels too low for this Arriver. The pithe olam (H6607, H5769), the ancient doors, predate the city's kings; the melek ha-kabod (H3519) outranks the doors themselves.

8.text: Who is this King of glory? The LORD, strong and mighty; the LORD, the mighty One in battle!
8.amp: Who is this King [melek] of glory [kabod]? The LORD [YHWH] strong [izzuz] and mighty [gibbor], the LORD mighty in battle [milchamah].
8.notes: The gatekeeper's challenge and the herald's answer, antiphonal: YHWH izzuz ve-gibbor (H5808, H1368) — the warrior returning with the ark from victory. The question is liturgy, not ignorance: asked so the Name can be proclaimed.

9.text: Lift up your heads, O you gates! Lift them up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in!
9.amp: Lift up [nasa] your heads [rosh], O ye gates [shaar]; even lift them up, ye everlasting [olam] doors [petach]; and the King [melek] of glory [kabod] shall come in [bo].
9.notes: The summons repeated whole — processions move by antiphon, the demand sounding at each gate in turn. The early church sang these verses of the ascension: heaven's own everlasting doors lifting for the Conqueror coming home (cf. Acts 1:9-11; Ephesians 4:8).

10.text: Who is He, this King of glory? The LORD of Hosts — He is the King of glory! Selah.
10.amp: Who is this King [melek] of glory [kabod]? The LORD [YHWH] of hosts [tsaba — of Armies], He is the King of glory. Selah [selah].
10.notes: The second challenge draws the fullest title: YHWH tsebaoth (H6635), Lord of every host in heaven and earth — the name that ends discussion. 'HE is the King of glory': the pronoun lands like a gavel, and Selah holds the gate open on the sight.
